papers.summary: DisMUSE develops distributed singular-spectrum optimization with Muon-style orthogonalized momentum, convergence guarantees, and a low-rank momentum-transmission variant for communication efficiency.
papers.relevance: Direct fit for spectral optimization, Newton-Schulz/Muon methods, convergence, and communication-quality tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: Distributed SSB optimization is still at an early stage, with open questions about convergence guarantees and communication efficiency.
communication-efficient variant based on low-rank (LR) momentum transmission

papers.title: DisMUSE: An Efficient Distributed Singular-Spectrum-Based Optimization Approach with Theoretical Convergence Guarantee

papers.summary: Studies matrix-factorization gradient flow with finite Newton-Schulz depth and shows that depth affects early rank selection and can change which stationary point the trajectory reaches.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses Newton-Schulz dynamics, rank selection, and optimization geometry.

evidence.quote: the number of Newton-Schulz steps can change the rank selected during the early stages of training

papers.title: Finite Spectral Depth Controls Gaussian Entrance Rank and Avoidance of the First Gradient-Flow Saddle

papers.summary: ResQAdam combines low-rank adaptive updates with a sign residual for QAT, reducing optimizer-state memory while preserving quality and throughput across several LLM scales and QAT settings.
papers.relevance: Strongest direct match for memory-efficient LLM optimization, low-rank optimizer states, model quality, peak memory, and throughput.

evidence.quote: It reduces optimizer-state memory by 71% to 74% relative to AdamW, stays close to AdamW in most settings, and lowers training throughput by less than 2%.
In from-scratch QAT, every baseline is far behind ResQAdam in both quantization settings

papers.title: ResQAdam: Residual-Preserving Adaptive Optimization for Memory-Efficient Quantization Aware Training

papers.summary: GEAR uses tangent-normal geometry and normal-spectrum estimates to expand LoRA rank in directions predicted to provide the largest local gain.
papers.relevance: Direct fit for dynamic LoRA rank evolution, spectral information, and low-rank optimization geometry.

evidence.quote: the leading normal singular directions yield the locally optimal rank expansion

papers.title: From What Is Used to What Is Missing: Rethinking Dynamic Rank in LoRA

papers.summary: Analyzes singular spectra and subspace motion of LoRA updates in supervised fine-tuning versus reinforcement learning, attributing differences partly to group-mean baseline subtraction.
papers.relevance: Directly matches interests in LoRA spectral dynamics, optimization behavior, and differences between training regimes.

evidence.quote: Tracking the singular spectrum and subspaces of LoRA updates

papers.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning

papers.summary: HiLo replaces adapter transmission with compressed gradient dissemination and local optimizer replay, while Spar uses spectral truncation, adaptive rank allocation, and error feedback.
papers.relevance: Strong fit for low-rank synchronization, communication cost, bandwidth-constrained training, and quality tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: decouple training rank from communication cost
transmitting as little as 1.6% of the adapter bytes, and accelerates end-to-end updates by up to 2.2× under bandwidth constraints

papers.title: Train High, Ship Low: Efficient LoRA Synchronization for Distributed On-Policy Post-Training

papers.summary: BiMuon applies Muon-style orthogonalized matrix updates to stochastic bilevel optimization and analyzes spectral imbalance and iteration complexity.
papers.relevance: Relevant to matrix-aware optimization, Muon, spectral geometry, and theoretical convergence.

evidence.quote: the lower-level (LL) problem curvature can induce significant spectral imbalance in the upper-level (UL) geometry
an O(ε^{-4}) iteration-complexity guarantee

papers.title: BiMuon: A Geometry-Aware Stochastic Bilevel Optimization Approach

papers.summary: SaMA generalizes Kronecker-based PEFT to obtain rank scaling beyond standard LoRA and analyzes how its invariance geometry affects optimizer behavior.
papers.relevance: Directly concerns low-rank PEFT, effective rank, optimizer-friendly geometry, and parameter-efficiency tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: its invariance manifold induces flat directions in the loss landscape, creating an optimization bottleneck for adaptive optimizers
its effective rank scales only linearly with the parameter budget

papers.title: SaMA: Morpho Adaptation via Asymmetric Expansion of Kronecker Product

papers.summary: Presents a forward-only LLM adaptation method that uses SVD-component activation geometry to select matrices and components for rank reduction.
papers.relevance: Relevant to SVD-based compressibility, rank reduction, adaptation memory, and speed at LLM scale.

evidence.quote: our forward-only search then efficiently identifies the weight matrix with the highest dispersion that merits rank reduction
theoretical analysis shows lower peak memory and greater speedup than the gradient-based approach

papers.title: Efficient LLM Adaptation with Forward-Only Passes

papers.summary: SCALAR learns scalar coefficients over fixed task-calibrated directions, achieving LoRA-comparable performance with fewer trainable parameters, lower memory, and higher throughput.
papers.relevance: Strong fit for parameter-efficient adaptation and practical memory-throughput tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: SCALAR achieves performance comparable to LoRA with substantially fewer trainable parameters, lower peak training memory, and higher throughput.
On commonsense reasoning, SCALAR achieves accuracy comparable to LoRA with about 4% of its trainable parameters.

papers.title: Direction or Magnitude? Learning Scalars over Task-Calibrated Directions

papers.summary: Defines behavioral rate as the compressed adapter size needed to preserve fine-tuning behavior and studies how it depends on the dataset-receiver pair and correction spectra.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses behavioral compressibility, adapter compression, singular directions, and noisy-data effects.

evidence.quote: fine-tuning compressibility is a property of the dataset--receiver pair rather than of the dataset alone
correction spectra measured on the data are able to rank these rates within a receiver

papers.title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information

papers.summary: Studies temporary weight decay in Muon-trained Transformers across model scales and shows delayed, scale-dependent effects mediated by persistent weight-norm changes.
papers.relevance: Direct fit for regularization, Muon optimization, norm dynamics, and training-scale tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: temporary weight decay in Muon-trained decoder-only Transformers
a schedule selected at 162M and transferred without retuning to 1.4B is 0.26 nats worse than no decay when removed

papers.title: Delayed Effects of Temporary Weight Decay in Muon Pretraining

papers.summary: DictLLM performs post-training LLM compression using shared SVD dictionaries, sparse coefficients, and component-specific quantization.
papers.relevance: Strong fit for low-rank weight compressibility, SVD structure, quantization, and memory-quality tradeoffs.

evidence.quote: Post-training compression is an effective approach to managing this trade-off
we obtain shared dictionaries via singular value decomposition (SVD) of input-scaled weight matrices

papers.title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels

papers.summary: Provides a theoretical analysis of Muon for Transformer next-token prediction, including spectral margins, convergence rates, learned weight structure, and generalization.
papers.relevance: Directly matches spectral optimization theory for LLM training and generalization.

evidence.quote: we characterize the optimization trajectory exactly and show that the normalized spectral margin is optimal after each update
we establish nonasymptotic convergence rates for the training loss and the normalized margin gap

papers.title: Theoretical Analysis of Muon on Transformers for Next-Token Prediction

papers.summary: LIRA allocates LoRA rank dynamically using second-order loss-perturbation estimates and displacement-based rank reallocation under matched budgets.
papers.relevance: Direct fit for interpretable dynamic rank allocation, low-rank parameterizations, and optimization-aware rank behavior.

evidence.quote: A More Interpretable Dynamic Loss-Informed Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation
LIRA scores each layer by the estimated magnitude of the local loss perturbation associated with its recent LoRA-factor movements under a second-order approximation

papers.title: LIRA: A More Interpretable Dynamic Loss-Informed Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation
